name: Gilt market
summary: UK inflation rose to 3.6% in October, below the BoE forecast; markets cut December rate-rise odds to 80%
state: ONS data on 18 Nov showed UK CPI at 3.6% in October, up from 3.5% and a one-year high, but below the Bank of England's 3.7% forecast; core held at 2.8% (Reuters via RTÉ). Markets trimmed the chance of a December Bank Rate rise to 80% from 90%. The 10-year yield reached above 5.35% on 16 Nov; the monthly move stays inside the 40bp line but long yields remain elevated, so Watch is kept.
for_you: High gilt yields feed through to fixed mortgage pricing and government borrowing costs; those remortgaging are most exposed.
rubric_hit: 30y gilt near multi-decade highs; 10y monthly move < 40bp

sources.title: RTÉ — UK inflation rises to one-year high but markets trim rate hike bets
The Intermediary — Inflation rises to 3.6% in October

why: Gilt yields set UK mortgage rates and the government's borrowing costs; the 2022 LDI crisis showed how fast it can break.
drivers: Fiscal credibility, BoE policy, inflation, global bond moves, pension-fund flows.

rubric.alert: BoE intervention, or 10y moved > 75bp in a month.
rubric.watch: 30y gilt at multi-decade highs, or 10y moved 40–75bp in a month, or a weak auction.
rubric.normal: 10y gilt moved < 40bp in a month and auctions orderly.
